panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Shows a small bronchus dilated with its lumen surrounded by fibrosis, consistent with the target disease. B: Demonstrates BO lesions localized to a membranous bronchiole, showing luminal narrowing. C: Shows complete obliteration of the membranous bronchiolar lumen due to disease. D: Shows a more distal bronchiole dilated compared to the obliterated proximal one, indicating distal airway changes.

panels.figure_caption: Comparison between macroscopic and full-scale microscopic appearance of the left superior horizontal bronchiole. (A) A small bronchus was dilated and the lumen surrounded by fibrosis. (B) The localization of the BO lesions with airway luminal narrowing was mainly observed in a membranous bronchiole corresponding to macroscopic appearance of a whitish small nodule. (C) The membranous bronchiolar lumen was completely obliterated. (D) The more distal bronchiole than the membranous bronchiole was dilated. (arrows) (Scale bar = 1 mm) (Elastic van Gieson stain).
in_text_mentions: ed with macroscopic and full-scale microscopic appearance of the left superior horizontal bronchiole, the localization of the BO lesions with airway luminal narrowing were mainly observed in membranous and more proximal bronchioli corresponding to macroscopic appearance of a whitish small nodule. After the membranous bronchiolar lumen was completely obliterated, again the more distal bronchiole than the membranous bronchiole was dilated. As a result, the occlusion of the bronchiole was located discretely (Figure 2). No other abnormalities were seen in the systemic organs other than both lungs.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Histopathological reconstruction of a small bronchus showing mild infiltration and replacement of epithelium by goblet cells, consistent with bronchiolitis pathology. B: Shows hallmark findings of constrictive bronchiolitis: prominent concentric fibrosis leading to luminal occlusion in the membranous bronchioles. C: Demonstrates elastic fiber proliferation (fibrotic changes) in distal bronchioli.
panels.attribution_text: Sugino et al. Bronchiolitis obliterans associated with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome: histopathological bronchial reconstruction of the whole lung and immunohistochemical study.. Diagnostic pathology 2013. doi:10.1186/1746-1596-8-134. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Microscopic bronchial reconstruction. (A) Small bronchi were dilated with mild infiltration of small round inflammatory cells and their epitheliums were replaced by goblet cell hyperplasia. (Scale bar = 500 μm) (Elastic van Gieson stain). (B) The prominent concentric fibrosis with mild infiltration of small round inflammatory cells was present in the submucosal layers, resulting in membranous bronchiolar luminal narrowing and complete occlusion. (Scale bar = 500 μm) (Elastic van Gieson stain). (C) The marked proliferation of elastic fibers, lack of inflammatory cells infiltration was observed in the more distal than membranous bronchioli. (Scale bar = 200 μm) (Elastic van Gieson stain).
in_text_mentions: sis with mild infiltration of small round inflammatory cells was present in the submucosal layers, resulting in membranous bronchiolar luminal narrowing and complete occlusion. In addition, the marked proliferation of elastic fibers with a few inflammatory cells infiltration was observed in the more distal bronchioli than membranous bronchioli. Some BO lesions were sporadically and intermittently located with varying degrees of narrowing and/or obliteration from the small bronchi to the membranous bronchioli. There was no evidence of BO lesions in respiratory bronchioli and alveoli (Figure 3).
